comment: Glyphs are CONTENT, like materials.json and reactions.json — not look-and-feel knobs like tuning.json. A glyph is a word of the ancient language: speaking it pushes a value on the caster VM's typed stack, and the cast key applies 'cast' to whatever is on top. Materials are referenced BY NAME and resolved to 12-bit ids at load (game/spell.cpp); a name that does not resolve is a LOUD error, never a silent id 0. Hot-reloads on R alongside materials.json. Types: element (names a material), form (turns the stack into a live effect), modifier (decorates the spell). Costs are integer mana — the VM is integer throughout so a spell is replayable and lockstep-safe (DESIGN.md §8).
language: EVERY sequence compiles into something that does something; there is no invalid spell, only one that does something other than you meant. Two rules make that true. (1) REPETITION AMPLIFIES: the Nth utterance of a glyph contributes 2^(N-1) and costs 2^(N-1) times its mana, so 'sand'=x1, 'sand sand'=x2, 'sand sand sand'=x4 — each extra word costs as much as everything before it, which is what makes repetition a real decision rather than a tedious ramp. Capped at 64x. A DIFFERENT element replaces rather than stacks ('water lava' throws lava): an element is what the spell is MADE of, and 'made of two things' has no meaning, whereas 'more of it' does. (2) AN UNSPOKEN FORM IS SPRAY: a bare element flings a few loose voxels of itself out of your hand, so the shortest legal spell is one word and every longer sequence is an elaboration of it.

budgets.comment: Rule 2 applied to magic: every sustained effect declares a FINITE budget up front, so no spell can hold a chunk awake forever. These are hard engine ceilings; a glyph's own budget is clamped to them at load. The spray* values are the DEFAULT FORM — what a bare element does when no form glyph was spoken. sprayVoxels is per cast at x1; repeating the element doubles it (sand=3, sand sand=6, sand sand sand=12), and maxSprayVoxels is the hard cap that keeps an amplified spray from crowding gore and debris shatter out of the shared per-tick particle spawn budget.

glyphs.desc: The word for water. Alone it is only a name; give it a form and it moves.
Molten stone. Expensive, and it does not care whose flesh it lands on.
Eats stone and meat alike. Backfiring on acid turns the speaker into it.
The cheapest matter there is. Good for practising without dying.
Hurls the spell from the caster's hand. speed is voxels/tick in 24.8 fixed point; lifetimeTicks bounds it absolutely (rule 2).

Lays the spell's element behind the projectile. voxelBudget is a hard VOLUME budget (an op of radius r costs (2r+1)^3), not an op count, so a fat trail costs proportionally more; when it runs out the trail stops and the projectile dies. That bound is what stops a trail spell pinning chunks awake. radius 0 = one voxel per mark: at 48 voxels/tick a radius-1 mark costs 27 voxels, so anything wider spends the whole budget within a tick or two and reads as a blob rather than a trail.

Converts what the projectile hits into the spell's element, via the same melt-mode overwrite BrushOp the laser uses. Target material is the element on the stack — 'acid transmute projectile' throws a bolt that turns rock to acid.

conjoined.comment: STUB (§G). A conjoined glyph is nothing but a saved list of glyph ids that pushes the same result as speaking them in order — no new VM opcode, no crafting UI yet. Present so the data model and the loader already carry the shape.

entries.desc: The worked example: a lava bolt that leaves a burning wake.
Turns whatever it strikes into acid, which then does the rest on its own.

wards.comment: STUB (§G). Wards are NOT implemented — this block only fixes the shape. Intended semantics: a ward filters the incoming OP STREAM on the CPU (cheap, sim untouched), never the CA itself. So a ward stops someone CASTING acid at your feet; it does not stop acid already flowing toward you. That is deliberate — it keeps the falling-sand game underneath, and makes 'cast next to them and let physics do it' the counterplay. drainFraction reduces EFFECTIVE MAX MANA by a FRACTION (per-mille here, integer like everything else): a flat cost would let a big late-game pool buy invulnerability, whereas a fraction keeps a ward a real choice at every scale.

entries.desc: Refuses transmutation ops targeting cells within radius of the warded caster.
Absorbs incoming projectiles before they resolve their impact.
